dimensions.no_issue_explanation: The supplied passages do not establish a specific literature-positioning concern. The authors identify their contribution as an extension of Transformer self-attention, acknowledge deterministic and learned position encodings, and explicitly cite prior attention weights biased by distance (Parikh et al., 2016). They also acknowledge graph attention (Veličković et al., 2017) when discussing storage concerns. Their contribution includes learned pairwise edge representations and a decomposition for efficient computation, rather than an explicit claim to have originated all uses of distance in attention. The discussion attributes the sinusoidal extrapolation motivation to the original Transformer authors. Although the abstract mentions generalization to graph-labeled inputs, the introduction and conclusion identify graph modeling as future work, so these passages do not support treating graph performance as an asserted experimental result. The supplied reference entries are consistent with the named citations at a bibliographic level. Assessing whether the technical distinctions from those works are sufficient would require their original texts; the present evidence does not justify manufacturing a novelty or citation concern.
